  What will be the biggest breakthrough of the next 50 years? As
  part of our 50th anniversary celebrations we asked over 70 of
  the world's most brilliant scientists for their ideas:

  Paul Davies forecasts the future
  The director of a new cosmic think tank is passionate about
  alien life, and suspects we may well find it soon.
  http://tinyurl.com/uept6
  Chris McKay forecasts the future
  A "second genesis" of life! We may find evidence of alien life
  frozen in Martian permafrost or on other worlds, perhaps dead
  but preserved
  http://tinyurl.com/yx3ah9
  Freeman Dyson forecasts the future
  We have been searching alien life for 50 years and found
  nothing, but in the next half century we shall discover it
  http://tinyurl.com/y36ejt
  Monica Grady forecasts the future
  Many theories predict that at least Mars and Europa are suitable
  hosts for life within our solar system - it will be
  disappointing if our increasingly sophisticated tools fail to
  find some
  http://tinyurl.com/y7kbxy
  Piet Hut forecasts the future
  The discovery of life elsewhere in the universe would be the
  most significant breakthrough, not only for astrophysics, but
  also for biology, philosophy and culture
  http://tinyurl.com/vvxoz
  Colin Pillinger forecasts the future
  We have been promised humans on Mars for so long now that I
  almost despair that this will be achieved by 2056, but we should
  at least have brought back Martian samples
  http://tinyurl.com/y6tklr
  Carolyn Porco forecasts the future
  The most significant development in planetary exploration in the
  next 50 years will be the discovery of either extant or
  fossilised extraterrestrial life forms on another solar system
  body

  "human" explication with possible "unknown" factors involved,
  i.e., the craft's propulsion system.

  of propulsion, in lay person's terms, this "changes" the rules
  as we know them.

  UFOs; physics tells us that based on a "person's mass" this
  action would kill a human being; assuming there are occupants in
  these craft, and they are similar to us, one might surmise that
  their "mass is changed" (decreased) in someway.(Possibly by
  their propulsion systems).
  If in fact any of the above is true, (and I believe it should be
  considered) then the "action/reaction" laws of physics may not
  apply, or at the very least would be altered in some way;
  henceforth we cannot assume that a "port-side outward explosion"
  in such a craft would react in the way we might expect.
  On the other hand your location is as good as any to begin
  searching. :>)

  >>Mass is not weight. Speed (strictly, veolocity) x mass = momentum.
  >Quite so. Moreover, the response of the soil to the impact would
  >involve a number of factors in addition to the debris momentum,
  >one being the effective areal density of the debris (essentially
  >its total mass divided by its projected area along the velocity
  >vector). The fact that the material was very lightweight does
  >not preclude a cratering/gouging response. A proper assessment
  >would include the total mass, speed, angle of incidence, and
  >orientation of the debris at impact, as well as at least some
  >soil properties (e.g., bulk density and degree of saturation).
  >If the estimated speed mentioned in the unsnipped post (400-500
  >mph) is accurate, and there were numerous debris fragments with
  >random orientations, it is likely that at least some of them
  >were quite deeply buried (at least several meters), irrespective
  >of whether any significant cratering occured. Somewhere I have a
  >code adapted from work done at Sandia that estimates penetration
  >in various soil types, but I can't find it on this hard drive.
  >I'll see if I can track it down.

  To All Interested in the Gouge at the Foster Impact Site: Dr.
  Dolman claims in his excavation report that the gouge the team
  dug was in fact an old coyote hole. Dr. Dolman, of the
  University of New Mexico - Archaeology Dept., and a contract
  archaeologist, had the final word. The "gouge" is a coyote hole.
  Not an artefact of any thing crashing.

  There are many first edition or limited printed UFO books that
  are now hard to find used copies of. Many of these books are not
  as old as Adamski's books such as 'UFO Crash at Aztec' by
  William Steinman and Wendelle Stevens (1985) or 'UFOs, MJ-12,
  and the Government' by Grant Cameron and T. Scott Crain (1991)
  which are much more factual and very enlightening. Many of the
  old UFO books in my large collection were found in second-hand
  book stores too, including church and garage sales, flea
  markets, etc.
  Like with any collectable hobby, the price a book will fetch
  does not depend on its rarity. For example, I have rare ancient
  coins and old sports cards that are worth less than some of the
  newer ones I have. A quick check with AbeBooks.com today came up
  with prices ranging between $3.00 to $22.65 for Adamski's 1967
  'Behind the Flying Saucer Mystery' while for his 1955 'Inside
  the Space Ships' ranged from $2.99 to $100.00 ($35.00 to $99.99
  for those copies signed by Adamski himself).

  Nick Balaskas

  his tale as certain investigations began to bear fruit.
  Bill McDonald's work, based on his discussions with Kaufmann
  (though the design more closely resembles some of the craft
  being developed at the Skunk Works is certainly interesting),
  must be examined carefully because Kaufmann lied. There is now
  no evidence that he was anything more than a personnel clerk who
  jumped on the Roswell bandwagon for personal gain.....
  So, arguing that the MP's story agrees with Kaufmann's is not
  advancing your cause but weakening it.
  And, for those keeping score at home, the shape of Arnold's
  craft, as seen in his original drawings looks like the heel of a
  boot, but in later drawings has taken on a crescent shape that
  has little resemblance to his first drawings... not that I want
  to begin a long discussion about the Arnold sighting. I'm merely
  making an observation that would tend to suggest that the MP's
  story is in conflict with other testimonies... some of which Ed
  has introduced.

  KRandle

  matter usually renders limited satisfaction to all sides of the
  argument.
  Fairness and subtlety often given up in exchange to meet rapid
  deadlines. It certainly helps if the producer has some
  insightful suggestions and is drawn to the subject matter with
  some knowledgeable forethought; With anything less he/she may be
  convinced to leave some of the best material on the editing
  floor or find it entertainingly distasteful to provide a voice
  to the middle ground.
  Hopefully, if done correctly, rendering a conclusion from a
  controversial broadcast is left in equal measure to both
  broadcaster and viewer alike. And, it certainly helps if enough
  new questions are raised that leave enough residual doubt on
  each side of a debate, forcing them at least to admit that it
  can never really hurt to dig a little deeper.

  of who, what, when, where and how the subject developed. If a
  person interested in the subject doesn't know the history, they
  are wasting their time on anything new.

  generations.

  eliminate the perception that just because a filmmaker makes a
  film or two on Ufology, doesn't mean the filmmaker is an expert.

  levels on UpDates off the scale.

  Kentucky and the re-enactment of the "Washington UFO flap of
  July 25-26th, 1952" and the White House Flying Saucer
  overflights are classics.
  This film, without a doubt, 'kick started' my interest and
  fascination with Ufology in 1956 and today, 50 years later, it
  is as fresh as the day I first saw it.

Closure Of Mystery Park Is No Enigma


                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2006 > Nov > Nov 19

                                             Closure Of Mystery Park Is No Enigma
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Sun, 19 Nov 2006 12:13:50 -0500
  Fwd Date: Sun, 19 Nov 2006 12:13:50 -0500
  Subject: Closure Of Mystery Park Is No Enigma


  Source: NZZ Online - Zurich, Switzerland
  http://www.nzz.ch/2006/11/19/eng/article7266028.html
  19. November 2006

  Closure Of Mystery Park Is No Enigma
  Alexander Kunzle - Swissinfo
  The demise of the Mystery Park in the Bernese Oberland resort of
  Interlaken, which closes on Sunday, is no enigma but the result
  of bad decisions, experts say.
  They argue that the main reasons for the closure are the static
  nature of the exhibition, the slow involvement of local tourism
  and the stock exchange decline between 2001 and 2003.
  "Mystery Park needs extraterrestrial saviour" and "Career
  dreamer Erich von Daniken pulls back" were just two of the
  sarcastic headlines journalists made in a long series of
  negative reports.
  The criticism stepped up in 2005 and was particularly heavy in
  the spring of 2006 when the park had to ask for a delay in
  bankruptcy proceedings and protection from its creditors.
  It all began in 1997 with ambitious plans. Best-selling Swiss
  author Erich von Daniken announced he wanted to open a theme
  park devoted to unsolved (extra-)terrestrial mysteries on the
  site of the former local military airport.
  As an international personality and mystery expert whose books
  have been translated into numerous languages, von Daniken
  appeared to be a guarantee that the park would be managed
  professionally.
  UFO image
  But Hannes Imboden, the former Bernese Oberland tourism
  director, said the communications department of the Mystery Park
  did not correct the one-sided UFO image that most people have of
  von Daniken.
  A similar assessment comes from the current director, Fritz
  Zemp, who has been at the mystery park since April 2005.
  "The marketing segment to target was not systematically
  approached at the outset," Zemp said. "What was more important
  entertainment, focusing on the UFO element of the hard core of
  von Daniken followers, or learning and education aspects?"
  After critical financial questions, the park opened its doors in
  May 2003. As the banks declined to provide money, the finances
  came from a group of private investors and the public who bought
  shares at a low par value despite the troubles at the stock
  exchange.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m19-011.shtml[12/12/2011 09:13:30]
Closure Of Mystery Park Is No Enigma


  "Von Daniken was unable to put into place what he'd really
  wanted," Thomas Vaszary, a lecturer at Lucerne's tourism
  college, told swissinfo.
  "It seemed a bad realisation of von Daniken's ideas. It lacked
  life and interaction."
  At the beginning Imboden had advised that at least a third of
  the park's exhibition should be changeable, a strategy that
  might have encouraged people to make return visits.
  Lack of life
  Zemp also felt there was a lack of life in the park.
  "Technically it would have been easy to change the software and
  hardware to counter the statics of the exhibition," he said.
  Christian Laesser, deputy director of the St Gallen Institute
  for Tourism, criticised a lack of innovation after the park had
  been built.
  He said that successful parks were those that continuously
  developed like, for example, the Europa-Park in Rust, Germany.
  "Only that [kind of development] maintains a steady flow of
  visitors," he told swissinfo.
  Zemp said there were many professional providers of tourist
  services in the Bernese Oberland ? the Jungfrau Railways, many
  hotels, adventure firms and tour operators ? that would have
  been possible partners for the park.
  He said the Mystery Park had only begun very late to offer
  packages that included meals and overnight stays.
  The park's financing ran into difficulties and was not helped by
  falls on the stock market. There were also groups of small and
  large shareholders that had different interests, according to
  Zemp.
  The fate of the Mystery Park now lies with the liquidator, who
  Zemp feels will probably put forward a number of proposals at
  next month's meeting of creditors.
  Insolvency proceedings are due to end on January 10. If none of
  the suggestions are accepted by the creditors, the park will be
  auctioned.

                                         UFO Reported During Grand Prix In Mexico
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Sun, 19 Nov 2006 11:15:59 -0500
  Fwd Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2006 09:59:10 -0500
  Subject: UFO Reported During Grand Prix In Mexico

  The Journal of Hispanic Ufology
  November 19, 2006
  Source: www.analuisacid.com
  Date: 11.18.06
  Mexico: UFO Reported During Grand Prix
  Mexican researcher Alfonso Salazar reports that on Sunday,
  November 12, 2006 at 13:30 hours, several people located on the
  ninth row of the grandstand of the Hermanos Rodriguez Speedway
  reported the transit of an amorphous, red-colored flying object
  traveling in a west-to-east direction over Mexico City at some
  3000 meters, separated by half a kilometer, approximately, from
  the Bell 206 helicopter that was engaging in aerial photography
  at the time, according to witness reports.
  The sighting took place during the pace lap performed by the
  racecar drivers shortly before the race began.
  This is the second time that a UFO report has taken place duirng
  the Mexico Grand Prix. The first was in 2003, when several
  people reported the manifestation of a metallic sphere suspended
  at a height over the city, also at the start of the race. At the
  time, it ws a Brazilian news crew who noticed the event and
  their report appeared on a news website in that country, with
  information supplied by journalist Sandro Borges.
  The current report concerning the alleged UFO over the Hermanos
  Rodriguez Speedway will be discussed by researcher Alfonso
  Salazar during the "Alta Velocidad" racing program hosted by
  senior race-car commentator Rodolfo Sanchez Noya on ABC Radio.
  -----
  Translation (c) 2006. Scott Corrales, IHU
  Special thanks to Ana Luisa Cid

Re: Cosford 1993 - McGonagle


  A map may be of some help, but the way that the re-entry path is
  calculated inherently creates a margin of error, the scale of
  which I am ignorant. The trajectory calculation is based on spot
  observations (by radar or visually) and projected from the last
  series of observations. The calculations can only attempt to
  compensate for change in mass or direction following break-up,
  or buffeting effects on re-entry. The resulting ground track may
  have a margin of error in the order of +/- 30 miles at a guess.
  Gary may comment further on this, if he does I will convey his
  comments to this List. Others on this List may be able to offer
  a more qualified comment than I can.
  [Note: since writing the above, Gary Anthony advises that the
  ground track would be far narrower based on his repeated
  calculations, only 3-6 miles wide]

  Cheers,
  Joe

  Hello Stuart, List,
  I'd be interested to know your thoughts on this Stuart. For
  nearly 12 months, Smartgroups was suffering postal delays of up
  to 3 weeks. I think that part of the reason for Smartgroups'
  problems was due to spam or virus generated false subscriptions
  - the sheer volume generated so many bounces that Smartgroups
  systems couldn't cope with it.
  These delays will in themselves have caused people to lose
  interest - you can't have a meaningful discussion with erratic
  delays of 3 weeks.
  Before migrating the List (I took the decision in January of
  this year), I needed to remove any obsolete or otherwise invalid
  email addresses. This involved sending out messages to each of
  the 1,500+ registered members. After a couple of batches of
  messages, I discovered the scale of the problem - in the order
  of 80% of the messages bounced! To prevent further false
  subscriptions, I made the List "invitation only", meaning that I
  had to approve new subscriptions manually. In doing so I
  prevented in the order of 1000 new false subscriptions.
  By the time I had sent out all of the validation messages and
  allowed time for them to respond before removing the ones which
  didn't either respond positively or bounce, I finished up with
  214 valid registered members. This was at great personal effort
  and investment of valuable time.
  This is the second (and I hope the last) time that the List has
  migrated, and on each occasion, a solid core of people have
  taken the trouble to re-register. To my knowledge, no other UFO-
  related List has survived such trauma.
  On November the 1st (18 days ago) I migrated the List.
  Membership currently stands at 85.
  There are many possible reasons why the remainder haven't yet
  migrated. I could enumerate them here but it seems that I don't
  need to, as you somehow know the single reason why in the order

  A Testable Astronautical Theory For UFO Events by Roy Dutton
  I wonder if anyone has examined the theory proposed by
  Mr. Dutton, who thinks we can "predict" UFO paths/target zones,
  as they perform automated surveillance of Earth. Searching the
  archives of UFO UpDates List I only find it mentioned back in
  1997 and he has published updates to his work more recently in
  2001 and 2003:
  http://www.daviddarling.info/encyclopedia/U/UFOs_Dutton1.html
  http://www.daviddarling.info/encyclopedia/U/UFOs_Dutton2.html
  http://www.nidsci.org/essaycomp/dutton_ashpole.html

  Summary of Claimed Discoveries
  It is now possible to bring together all the elements of the
  Astronautical Theory for SAC/UFO Events, a theory encapsulating
  the following discoveries:
   - Strange aerial craft (SAC) displaying inexplicable
  characteristics, but described by reliable eyewitnesses, are
  physically real.
   - The SAC descend from the sky and depart back into it and
  display operational capabilities beyond our current
  understanding.
   - The SAC are atmospheric probes. They are deposited into the
  atmosphere by advanced spacecraft ("motherships") and are,
  later, retrieved by them.
   - All the fully automated craft are engaged in continuing
  Earth surveillance and exploration activities.
   - The hypothetical spacecraft motherships follow well-defined
  paths in space as they approach the Earth and then orbit
  transiently, at super-orbital speeds, to release the SAC over
  selected target zones on the Earth's surface before accelerating
  away.
   - The motherships' approach paths in space are governed by
  fixed (programmed) rules determining orbit inclination and
  celestial orientation.
   - Two kinds of celestial orientation have been identified. Two
  orientations are referenced to the fixed stars. The remaining
  two are linked to the position of the Sun amidst the stars and,
  therefore, move round the sky with the Sun throughout any year.
   - The presence of a solar system body (planet, minor planet,
  comet, etc.) in visual alignment with one of the programmed
  approach paths seems often to signal the choice of that path for
  the activity in hand.
  All of these claimed discoveries are now in great need of
  rigorous scientific investigation. In view of their potential

  importance and the weight of evidence supporting them, they
  surely warrant that kind of response, but to date there has been
  little movement in that direction.

  the right of the "s" in "Dobwalls". This appears much larger and

  shows the location and outline of the Lantoom quarry excavation

  this the excavation is located S of the A38 and W of a minor
  access road shown on all maps. This road links the excavation

  The excavation is centred on SX225649.

  junction. The grid ref of this point is SX228650 as close as can
  be judged, at 45m MSL with he A38 oriented very close to E-W.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m21-010.shtml[12/12/2011 09:14:08]
Re: Cosford 1993 - Shough

  The quarry proper (SX225649) is therefore approximately 300 yds
  WSW of the position of the witness.
  All of this means that if the lights passed directly overhead
  and were lost behind the Lantoom quarry they could not have been
  travelling N-S, still less NW-SE, but would have been travelling
  broadly NE-SW, so Brad is again correct.
  However this depends on the meaning of the sentence: "I lost
  sight of them owing to the high ground of the quarry this
  immediately on my left". From the Sgt's position the quarry
  proper is not "immediately on my left" but arguably that phrase
  is a more reliable indicator of relative position than "the high
  ground of the quarry" which might refer to (e.g) the general
  land owned by the quarry company rather than the actual
  excavation.
  On any hypothesis we would want to use the car as reference
  here, not the Sgt's own person, because if the Sgt is outside
  and turned to face the disappearing object it makes no sense to
  say that it disappeared "on my immediate left" rather than
  "directly ahead". There is high ground here on the immediate
  left (i.e. near side) of the parked car, rising from 45m MSL at
  the road to 136 m MSL in 400 yds due S of his position. In this
  case the objects were not heading SW but considerably E of that
  heading.
  This is not inconsistent consistent with the Sgt's estimate of a
  "dead straight N-S course". At the same time the above
  "correction" is in the right direction for what is needed to fit
  the track with the Cosmos booster, heading SE. It arguably
  doesn't go far enough, but a misjudgment of heading by 45 degs
  or so is possible.
  On the other hand it's true that a direction of SE (the Cosmos
  booster track) from the witness's position would miss the high
  ground immediately S of the witness. A SE bearing would be in
  the direction from which the witness has just driven, i.e. down
  the straight NW-SE stretch of the A38 running along the East
  Looe River valley. This is not a strong argument in itself
  because the topography isn't known in sufficient detail. The
  road runs in a cutting around this corner and there may be a
  high shoulder or embankment that in the dark was effectively
  part of the southern hillside referred to (my vague memory of
  the road is not helpful here).
  Another factor is the clarity of the cardinal directions here
  with respect to the E-W direction of the road running past the
  quarry to Dobwalls. This immediately stands out when looking at
  the map and I dare say this experienced local Sgt was aware of
  this orientation and judged the trajectory relative to the well-
  known road. It is correct that he was outside of the car before
  the objects climbed overhead and was able to watch them cross
  from one side of the road to the other without confusion caused
  by relative motion. One might reasonably expect that when he
  specifies a "dead straight S-N course" he meant what he said,
  not NW-SE.
  This would be consistent also with the Sgt's earlier description
  of the relative displacement of the objects in the windscreen as
  he was making the left turn. During the turn the object moved
  from his 2 o'clock to 1 o'clock as Brad points out. This is
  opposite to the tendency for an object which is truly stationary
  in relative azimuth, and a left turn would actually *accelerate*
  the apparent motion to the *right* (i.e towards 3 o'clock) of an
  object which was actually moving towards the right (W). This
  favours an object on a true heading S of his average line of
  travel rather than W of it.
  Of course the aforegoing assumes that the objects did pass
  through the zenith at "12 o'clock high". Maybe we have a bit
  more latitude here because the familiar reference frame of the
  E-W road doesn't apply and maybe "12 o'clock high" does really
  mean (say) "10 o'clock high". We know from many reports and from
  experiments that elevation angles are routinely overestimated,
  often drastically, so it's reasonable to suggest such a
  correction here. If the objects when "curving overhead" actually
  passed somewhat to the W of the Sgt's position, so that he was
  looking steeply up but not vertically, then they could have been
  on a NE-SW ballistic trajectory and still passed behind the high
  ground to the S as described, rather than down the East Looe


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m21-010.shtml[12/12/2011 09:14:08]
Re: Cosford 1993 - Shough

  River valley.
  One possible problem here is that a path to the W of the zenith
  for an observer here seems to conflict with the orbital elements
  for the Cosmos 2238 booster. Gary Anthony's calculated
  trajectory shown at
  http://www.mithrand.karoo.net/index.htm/cosford.htm
  appears well to the east of witnesses in this part of Cornwall:
  "The re-entry track traversed south-easterly over the UK,
  through Ireland and Devon [east of Cornwall] and may account for
  delineated and different directions in the official witness
  reports for the sightings at or near the 01:10 local time. The
  re-entry was observed from Ireland before crossing over the
  Irish Sea to Devon."
  The screen-grab of the computer simulation for 0110:03 BST shows
  the coordinates lat 50.47N long 4.20W. A NW-SE track passing
  through these coordinates (apparently within an error of less
  than +/- 3 miles) could not at any time pass to the W of the
  zenith for a witness at about 50.27N, 4.29W but would pass at
  high elevation to the E of the zenith, tending to strain the
  above explanation of how the objects could have passed behind
  the hill to the S rather than over the valley to the SE.
  So there are some aspects of this report that do not add up very
  satisfactorily, in addition to the reported 1-hour time
  discrepancy, and in isolation one might want to keep the case
  open.
  But the contemporaneous MoD report does relate the sighting to
  the same thing seen by other Devon and Cornwall police at 0110
  BST, and as others have asked, given the time why did this
  witness (and the others) not see a UFO _and_ a re-entering
  booster if the two things are distinct? It seems to me more
  economical to conclude (at present) that there is some error
  either in the report or in our interpretations of it, even if we
  can't identify exactly what it is.

  >>The Sergeant indicates it disappeared behind the Lantoom Quarry

  >I might be able to help here. I lived on Bodmin Moor nearby in
  >1989 and know this area a bit. I also have Ordnance Survey
  >Landranger 1:50,000 and Pathfinder 1:25,000 maps. ...
  >Brad is correct that SX230650 grid ref is just an area
  >approximation. The Sgt's account indicates that he drove around
  >the uphill bend from Looe Mills (SX232648) towards Dobwalls then
  >pulled up 100 yds short of the laybay at the Lantoon Quarry
  >junction. The grid ref of this point is SX228650 as close as can
  >be judged, at 45m MSL with he A38 oriented very close to E-W.
  >The quarry proper (SX225649) is therefore approximately 300 yds
  >WSW of the position of the witness.
  >All of this means that if the lights passed directly overhead
  >and were lost behind the Lantoom quarry they could not have been
  >travelling N-S, still less NW-SE, but would have been travelling
  >broadly NE-SW, so Brad is again correct....
  >On any hypothesis we would want to use the car as reference
  >here, not the Sgt's own person, because if the Sgt is outside
  >and turned to face the disappearing object it makes no sense to
  >say that it disappeared "on my immediate left" rather than
  >"directly ahead". There is high ground here on the immediate
  >left (i.e. near side) of the parked car, rising from 45m MSL at
  >the road to 136 m MSL in 400 yds due S of his position. In this
  >case the objects were not heading SW but considerably E of that
  >heading....
  >On the other hand it's true that a direction of SE (the Cosmos
  >booster track) from the witness's position would miss the high
  >ground immediately S of the witness. A SE bearing would be in


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m22-002.shtml[12/12/2011 09:14:12]
Re: Cosford 1993 - Sparks

  >the direction from which the witness has just driven, i.e. down
  >the straight NW-SE stretch of the A38 running along the East
  >Looe River valley....
  >Another factor is the clarity of the cardinal directions here
  >with respect to the E-W direction of the road running past the
  >quarry to Dobwalls. This immediately stands out when looking at
  >the map and I dare say this experienced local Sgt was aware of
  >this orientation and judged the trajectory relative to the well-
  >known road. It is correct that he was outside of the car before
  >the objects climbed overhead and was able to watch them cross
  >from one side of the road to the other without confusion caused
  >by relative motion. One might reasonably expect that when he
  >specifies a "dead straight [N-S] course" he meant what he said,
  >not NW-SE.
  >This would be consistent also with the Sgt's earlier description
  >of the relative displacement of the objects in the windscreen as
  >he was making the left turn. During the turn the object moved
  >from his 2 o'clock to 1 o'clock as Brad points out. This is
  >opposite to the tendency for an object which is truly stationary
  >in relative azimuth, and a left turn would actually *accelerate*
  >the apparent motion to the *right* (i.e towards 3 o'clock) of an
  >object which was actually moving towards the right ([E])....
  >One possible problem here is that a path to the W of the zenith
  >for an observer here seems to conflict with the orbital elements
  >for the Cosmos 2238 booster. Gary Anthony's calculated
  >trajectory shown at
  >http://www.mithrand.karoo.net/index.htm/cosford.htm
  >appears well to the east of witnesses in this part of Cornwall:
  >"The re-entry track traversed south-easterly over the UK,
  >through Ireland and Devon [east of Cornwall]...."
  >The screen-grab of the computer simulation for 0110:03 BST shows
  >the coordinates lat 50.47N long 4.20W. A NW-SE track passing
  >through these coordinates (apparently within an error of less
  >than +/- 3 miles) could not at any time pass to the W of the
  >zenith for a witness at about [50 27N, 4 29W] but would pass at
  >high elevation to the E of the zenith, tending to strain the
  >above explanation of how the objects could have passed behind
  >the hill to the S rather than over the valley to the SE.
  >So there are some aspects of this report that do not add up very
  >satisfactorily, in addition to the reported 1-hour time
  >discrepancy, and in isolation one might want to keep the case
  >open.
  The bottom line here is that thanks to Martin's excellent work
  in tracking down the Lantoom Quarry it is clear that the Quarry
  was to the S of the road the police Sgt was traveling. My
  reading of the Sgt's report was correct, that the Quarry was
  located to his south and left, and Joe M's strained
  interpretation that the Sgt was turned around is wrong.
  Joe argues that the Sgt's left was to the E and thus consistent
  with the reentering Cosmos 2238 rocket stage. But in fact the
  Sgt correctly related his left to the W (or southwest) over the
  Quarry where the objects disappeared, exactly as I had
  contended.
  That makes it extremely difficult to explain the Sgt's sighting.
  We cannot make it fit the Cosmos 2238 simply by changing one or
  two details. We would have to change ALL of the details and/or
  delete those details which simply do not fit by any reasonable
  scenario, such as eliminating the disappearance behind the
  Lantoom Quarry. Just get rid of that entirely if you want to
  make the Police Sgt's report fit C2238.
  I'd be more inclined to dismiss the Sgt's report if it was vague
  or just a sentence or two. But he has two pages of very minute
  details as to his position and the objects' position and how
  they changed. This does not seem dismissable and does not seem
  confused, and most of the rest of the sightings have problems as
  well. If he was confused one would expect to see evidence of
  confusion, such as contradictory details or omitting major
  points (such as, supposing hypothetically, he had forgotten to
  mention how the objects disappeared).

  seconds of latitude or longitude, which are for calculational
  comparison only. Also note that the amateur astronomer John
  Fitzsimons sighted the Cosmos 2238 reentry from Sligo, Ireland,
  where he saw it reach 70 degrees elevation (almost overhead) at
  close approach to his SW. This defines the reentry trajectory to
  go through a line about 20 miles to the SW of Sligo, which
  translates to shifting all of the tabulated positions above by
  about 1/3 to 1/2 degree longitude to the East, and requiring
  about 2 minute earlier times.
  Hence for the key positions at 0009 to 0011 Z time these would
  change to 0007 to 0009 as follows (with roundoffs):
  31 Mar 1993 00:07 53=B037' N 008=B0.4 W poss 100 km altitude
  31 Mar 1993 00:08 50=B037' N 004=B0 W possibly 80 km
  31 Mar 1993 00:09 47=B027' N 000=B0 W possibly 60 km
  This puts the Cosmos 2238 decay track from roughly Boyle,
  Ireland, to Dartmouth, Devon, England, to Angers, France, and
  these are larger towns chosen for ease of spotting on a map, not
  for exactness. These are _not_ the coordinates above
  necessarily, just closest large cities to a line through the
  above coordinates.

  Investigation Uncovers Spy Game Surrounding UFO Mystery

  Were secure vaults breached at Los Alamos, a USAF base, and

  A national security issue buried in a UFO tale has been
  interpreted to an official under the Office of the Director of
  National Intelligence. Starstream Research investigates in a new
  on-line feature series titled, "Exempt from Legal Recourse."
  Truth is often stranger than fiction. Nowhere is this more
  apparent than in the latest revelations detailed by the on-line
  investigative report produced by Starstream Research. I am the
  de facto editor and senior writer for Starstream Research, a
  private provider of intelligence and analysis on futuristic
  national and international defense, security and risk
  developments. I founded Starstream Research to explore areas of
  'exotic' technologies that often remain outside of the bounds of
  conventional intelligence publications, like those produced by
  the esteemed "Jane's Information Group." Exploring cutting edge
  and 'over the edge' topics, such as the application of cold
  fusion research for new weapons of mass destruction technology,
  or the U.S. Government's twenty-year interest in using
  parapsychology for intelligence collection, are the norm for
  Starstream Research. In other words, we often explore topics
  which Jane's might not touch with the proverbial "ten foot
  pole."
  Over the past few years Starstream Research has evolved from
  numerous contacts with scientists located around the world. They
  share a common vision of new and more advanced understanding of
  the laws of nature, and their application to practical
  technologies. As a result we have also bumped heads with members
  of the intelligence community, or their proxies in the private
  sector. Our latest series of stories, "Exempt from Legal
  Recourse," developed from sources working with the intelligence
  sector of the government.
  As editor of Starstream Research, I have been attempting to walk
  a thin line between sources' requests for anonymity and the need
  to move our investigation forward. The result has been something
  of a mixed bag, leaving both readers and sources less than
  satisfied with the details we have provided. I am in the process
  of reviewing a considerable amount of material, and determining
  what may and may not be released to the public.
  The present controversy revolves around stories released by
  Starstream Research, and distributed by The American Chronicle.
  Those stories revealed that in late August of this year, three

  independently confirmed by another unnamed source who requested
  not to be identified.

  release of personal and confidential email messages to an
  independent investigator close to Starstream Research, via Dan
  T. Smith, a private citizen who received copies forwarded from

  mutual undisclosed source confirmed that the issue was briefly
  brought before the FBI when reviewing national security
  clearance and procedure.

  cloak and dagger activities, both past and present. More

  told in his out of print book, "Penetration."

  presence,' there is no question that the tale has left a
  mysterious trail in official government records.

  purpose, not simply "expose'" morning coffee. You do excellent
  analysis. I sure as heck am learning things I didn't know, but

  to investigate

Re: Cosford 1993 - Sparks


  1. If the Sgt was on the part of road A38 heading NW then he
  could see something off to his 2 o'clock position, as he
  reported, which would be almost precisely to his due N. But
  Martin has written his posting (see original, not quoted above)
  as if the Sgt was making his Left curving turn where A38 curves
  to the W while he was having his sighting. I am not sure how he
  arrived at that conclusion. Was it from studying the location of
  the Quarry on the maps perhaps?
  One problem I see with that is that if the Sgt observed the two
  lights while in the middle of making a Left curving turn then
  the lights would appear to head off to his relative Right and as
  Martin pointed out they would go towards 3 o'clock position not
  1 o'clock (and then continuing on to 12 o'clock).
  If the Sgt was already past the Left curve and was heading W
  then his 2 o'clock position would be towards about the NNW and
  thus more consistent with Cosmos 2238 rocket's path and where it
  should have first appeared. But then the lights should have
  moved to the Sgt's Right, going from 2 o'clock to 3 o'clock to 4
  o'clock, and they did not do that according to his report.
  The lights instead moved from his 2 to 1 to 0 o'clock positions
  (0 o'clock is 12 o'clock, but easier to see the smooth
  progression when numbered 2 to 1 to 0).
  2. I am confused as to why anything would have been seen by the
  Sgt out towards the WSW at disappearance. The Quarry excavation
  to the WSW (from exactly where?) would not hide anything would
  it? Only the Quarry "high ground" to the S would block the view
  of the lights passing the overhead point heading S, right?
  >If the lights disappeared in the WSW and went near the
  >zenith at "12 o'clock high" they could not possibly have
  >been on a "dead straight North-South" trajectory. So this
  >would make the Sgt's evidence incoherent.
  As for "impossibility" of seeing a "dead straight North-South"
  trajectory offset to the WSW this is not a problem if it was in
  fact to the S not the WSW. As I questioned above, I do not see
  why a WSW direction enters into anything here at all. (A N-S
  trajectory can be seen off to one side but it is not a head-on
  or "dead straight" path in that case.)
  Keep in mind that the Sgt did not say the lights disappeared at
  _exactly_ 12 o'clock high position but indicates it was right
  afterward. One infers that since he did not mention an 11
  o'clock position that the lights disappeared somewhere between
  12 and 11 o'clock positions, as referenced to his original
  orientation of his patrol car (since he was now at this point
  outside his vehicle). This disappearance would have been to his
  S behind the high ground of the Quarry, if I understand Martin's
  mapping data correctly.
  >Gary Anthony has provided me some more data for the track
  >produced by his simulation. They are pretty close to those
  >provided by Brad. ...
  >The max elevation of this track would be about 80 degs in the NE
  >from Lantoom in Cornwall. This is pretty close to "12 o'clock
  >high" by any ordinary standards.
  But this is in the wrong direction for the Quarry to block the
  Sgt's view. The Quarry was to the S not to the NE. Why would the
  reentering Cosmos 2238 rocket have disappeared suddenly to his
  NE in clear skies? He said the Quarry blocked his view.
  Also my adjusted satellite ground track obtained from Alan
  Pickup would not agree with these figures from Martin, if it
  passed to the SW of the amateur astronomer John Fitzsimons in
  Sligo, Ireland, at 70 degrees elevation, as Fitzsimons reported.
  My adjusted track through that position would run about 20 miles
  E of the Sgt at about his 4 o'clock position, nowhere near his
  reported directions and nowhere near the Lantoom Quarry on the
  opposite side of the road to his S or W (depending on when and
  where we put the poor Sgt!).
  My rounded off estimated positions for the Cosmos 2238 rocket

http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m23-005.shtml[12/12/2011 09:15:14]
Re: Cosford 1993 - Sparks

  31 Mar 1993 00:07 53 37' N 008.4 W poss 100 km altitude
  31 Mar 1993 00:08 50 37' N 004 W possibly 80 km
  31 Mar 1993 00:09 47 27' N 000 W possibly 60 km
  (Please note that the altitudes in km given in the lengthy table
  supplied by Alan Pickup in my last posting, are idealized as if
  the satellite was not decaying. Alan explained that what happens
  at the point of the last orbit of reentry is that at perigee,
  the lowest point, the atmospheric drag is at its greatest. That
  is when it pulls down the satellite or space debris and _if_
  this is the terminal trajectory then it does not rise in
  altitude from perigee, or does not rsie much, but begins to
  descend. In this case the Cosmos 2238 rocket reached perigee of
  about 107 km above the earth's surface at about 2352 Z time,
  roughly 15-20 minutes before final burnup presumably over
  France.)
  >Perhaps the Sgt got out facing W then craned his
  >head right back and simultaneously swivelled
  >to watch the lights, passing high overhead almost behind
  >him, in such a way that he was slightly disorientated?
  This does not explain the continuity of the Sgt.'s directional
  data, with the lights moving from 2 to 1 to 0 o'clock (= 12
  o'clock), and again is the wrong side of the road for the Quarry
  to block his view so the objects could disappear.
  In trying to make this sighting fit Cosmos 2238, I have even
  considered the possibility that the Sgt somehow got his
  "o'clock" directions mirror reversed, perhaps he was even
  dyslexic. However that makes things even worse! If his 2 o'clock
  becomes 10 o'clock direction, then his 1 o'clock becomes 11
  o'clock and then 12 o'clock gets to remain the same, then from
  the direction of the heading of A38 road, the Sgt would have
  first sighted the objects to the S, moving N !!!
  >I accept that this report and the interlocking topographical
  >references do _suggest_ that he was describing a view framed by
  >a SW aspect, rather then the NE aspect that would seem more
  >natural given the ground track of the Cosmos booster. I can't
  >definitely explain why that should be so, but I still feel that
  >invoking a UFO plus a booster doesn't seem realistic. So some
  >sighting and/or reporting error, or some misinterpretation on
  >our part, remains the most likely explanation of apparent
  >discrepancies in this case, though I still find it interesting
  >to investigate them.
  >Martin Shough
  I am not saying it was a UFO either. I just can't make it nicely
  fit the Cosmos 2238. This is not a case of a vague, third-hand,
  one-line report but is a first-hand 2-page report with a great
  amount of spatial position detail. What was needed was an on-
  site investigation with an on-site timed, measured and
  calibrated reenactment of the whole sighting with the Sgt. When
  a witness provides such a large amount of specific detail with
  no apparent internal contradictions this would be worth singling
  out for a scientific on-site reenactment. You would not do that
  willy-nilly for all cases indiscriminately, for every two-bit
  worthless reports.
  This case is in a different league altogether and would have
  been worth serious study at the time it occurred. Maybe an in-
  person investigation at the time would have neatly resolved it
  into the Comsos 2238 and resolved the directional data that
  conflict with the reentry path. Whether an on-site investigation
  would be fruitful if carried out today 13 years after the fact
  is debatable, and we don't have the Sgt's name.

  Hello List,
  Would anyone care to recommend a breakdown of 'entities'
  encountered, classified by type? And maybe giving a geographical
  spread?
  I've recently been reminded of one particular type - smallish
  creatures described as biological and living but also variously
  said to be 'incomplete' 'damaged' 'with added organs' or
  'missing facial organs', also'distressed' or 'bereft'.
  Have the impression that these are geographically limited, most
  reports I've read seem to be from Latin America, with one or two
  from Italy and perhaps a few in Russia.
  There's a scenario - which I think is too complex for _all_
  isolated &/or naive witnesses to anticipate and contrive - that
  these are biologically engineered ('uplifted') entities used as
  agents, pilots, etc., and that they had been lost (or abandoned)
  after getting damaged or sick, or after their craft has gone
  down.
  Examples are Varghina-types (and chupacabras) in South America
  and Puerto Rico, and the Italian Caponi case described by Tim
  Good (which was apparently followed or preceded by a brief
  sighting of similar but flying (undamaged) entity in another,
  nearby, region of Italy).
  Recent reminder was Corso's weary but dogged repetition that he
  thought what he saw was not a humanoid but a 'thing' - a living
  part of the craft.
  That scenario has implications:- 1) we're being visited,
  observed by one or more races capable of quite skilled
  biological construction - which could be much cheaper than
  hi-tech; 2) they're not necessarily all that far ahead of us
  technology-wise - we could forecast similar capabilities in one
  or two hundred years or so; if we chose that path).
  And that at least one of those races don't seem very
  compassionate towards their own living creations.

  Cheers
  Ray D

                                                    Re: Cosford 1993 - McGonagle
  From: Joe McGonagle <joe.mcgonagle.nul>
  Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 05:47:13 +0000
  Fwd Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 21:29:28 -0500
  Subject: Re: Cosford 1993 - McGonagle

  Hello List,
  I shall be replying to Brad's post from a couple of days ago,
  and will be quoting extensively from the following transcription
  of the image of the documents at:
  http://www.uk-ufo.org/cosford/moo310110-2.gif
  and:
  http://www.uk-ufo.org/cosford/moo310110-3.gif
  I thought it would be useful for future reference in the UpDates
  archives to post a transcription of the document here, since it
  is possible that the files may be renamed or otherwise
  unavailable at a later date.
  Joe
  --- Begin transcription ---
  [Heading] Devon and Cornwall Constabulary
  [Subtitle] Witness statement
  Statement of [obliterated]
  Age if under 21: O 21 (if over 21 insert "over 21")
  This statement (consisting of 2 pages each signed by me) is true
  to the best of my knowledge and belief and I make it knowing
  that, if it is tendered in evidence, I shall be liable to
  prosecution if I have wilfully stated in it anything which I
  know to be false or do not believe to be true.
  Dated this 31st day of March 1993
  Signature [illegible signature]
  I am a sergeant in the Devon and Cornwall Constabulary stationed
  at Liskeard in Cornwall.
  At about 0110 hrs on the morning of Wednesday 31st of March 1993
  I was on duty in uniform and driving a marked police vehicle
  along the A38 at Looe Mills near Liskeard travelling in the
  direction of Dobwalls.
  This was naturally during the hours of darkness and the weather
  was fine and dry, with some patchy cloud; the moon and a number
  of stars being visible. I was unaccompanied.
  As I began to negotiate a sweeping uphill left hand bend at the
  bottom of Lantoom Hill, I became aware of what appeared to be
  two 'stars' just above the horizon in the approximate position
  of 'two o'clock'. They were due North of me and motionless in
  the sky. My attention was drawn to these 'stars' because apart
  from being in a part of the sky where there are usually no
  stars, they were of a darker hue bordering on yellow instead of
  silvery-white. They were reasonably close together but as I


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m24-005.shtml[12/12/2011 09:15:45]
Re: Cosford 1993 - McGonagle

  could not begin to estimate their distance from me, I likewise
  cannot estimate how far they were from each other.
  As I negotiated the bend I continued to observe them when I
  suddenly saw them begin to move what appeared to be vertically
  upwards. They maintained a parallel course and identical speed
  and as they approached the 'one o'clock' position they began to
  leave vapour trails. I brought my car to a halt, switched off
  the engine, and got out. My location now was
  Signature [obliterated] signature witnessed by [no signature]
  [second page]
  Form MG11A(T)
  Continuation sheet No. [not completed]
  Continuation of statement of [obliterated]
  approximately 100 yards the Liskeard side of the lay by outside
  Lantoom Quarry, map ref 230 650.
  My view of these objects was very good; the sky being clear, and
  they continued their Ascent still at an identical speed to each
  other and still on a parallel course. I realised that they were
  not ascending vertically but rather curving overhead and heading
  due South. As they gained in height the vapour trails became
  much more pronounced. I was still unable to estimate their
  height because of their small size (identical to a star in the
  night sky) but I believe they were very high. As they passed
  directly overhead at '12 o'clock high', the heavens at this
  point were bright and moonlit and I could see that there was
  nothing between the objects apart from empty sky. They were
  definitely two seperate objects.
  At about this time I became aware of what I believed to be a
  third object visible only by its vapour trail which was
  considerably less obvious than the vapour trail of the other two
  objects. This third object seemed to the right hand side of the
  left hand object (as I was looking up), and slightly to the rear
  of it. It maintained the identical speed and parallel course of
  the other objects.
  As the objects continued on a dead straight north south course,
  they seemed to be travelling at a similar speed to a high flying
  passenger jet aircraft. I lost sight of them owing to the high
  ground of the quarry immediately on my left.
  During the total duration of this sighting, which was between 45
  seconds an one minute, my observation of these objects was
  continuous and uninterrupted. There was no sound whatever, the
  night being very still with no traffic.
  Signature [obliterated] Signature witnessed by [not signed]
  --- End transcription ---

Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Aliens


                                                          UFO Updates
                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'
    Location: UFOUpDatesList.Com > 2006 > Nov > Nov 24

                                          Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Aliens
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 21:39:47 -0500
  Fwd Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 21:39:47 -0500
  Subject: Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Aliens


  Source: Featured Articles.Com - Sungai Buloh, Selangor, Malaysia
  http://tinyurl.com/ykynha
  23rd November 2006

  Aliens: Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Them
  Gersiane De Brito
  SETI, or Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence, has been an
  ongoing endeavor for many decades. In the early days, it was
  expected to be a quick success, so much so that national
  governments even helped fund these projects. Like the Moon race,
  there was something of a "find E.T." race. All that is gone now.
  Government funding has virtually evaporated around the globe.
  The explanation is simple: no one likes a perpetual failure. The
  few remaining SETI efforts have to count on private funding to
  scrape along. Well, the objective of this article is to come to
  the rescue of the last of the SETI astronomers, to tell them
  where they can find E.T. so that they can regain the world's
  respect.
  That last sentence was not meant to be cynical. As noted in my
  article "Decoding Book Resurrects the Ancient Astronaut Theme,"
  author Morten St. George claims that some of the prophecies of
  Nostradamus are of alien origin, and that those prophecies tell
  us how to calculate the galactic coordinates of where E.T. came
  from. In a follow-up interview, I posed the following question
  to St. George: Do you agree that contact with intelligent aliens
  could be of immense importance to humankind? He agreed. Then I
  asked: Do you agree that this is more important than your
  selling a few copies of your cryptic thinking book? He agreed.
  This article will be a little longer and a little more technical
  than the others.
  According to St. George, three prophetic stanzas combine to
  provide information about E.T.'s location. The first of these is
  stanza number I-81. Here, the first four words of the fourth
  verse are the most relevant: "Kappa, Thita, Lambda, mors." St.
  George says he has an etymological dictionary that defines
  "mors" as the "bite of a scorpion." Consequently, Kappa, Theta,
  and Lambda are the names of three stars in the tail section of
  the constellation Scorpius. (Note that the use of Greek letters
  for star names postdates Nostradamus). It's a star arrow, and
  Lambda is the arrow head. Elsewhere, the prophecies name three
  cities to form an arrow circling around the globe; thus, St.
  George believes the three stars should be viewed as points on a
  sphere.
  Where does the star arrow point? St. George says he followed the
  star arrow upwards on a star map and it hit or passed close to a
  dark cloud called Barnard 72, for which he already had other
  indications. So that's the answer. E.T. came from or near
  Barnard 72. But we're not done yet. We're looking for precise
  coordinates.


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m24-006.shtml[12/12/2011 09:15:45]
Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Aliens

  The second stanza is numbered IV-32. According to St. George's
  decoding, this stanza tells a story: Once upon a time, Triton,
  Pluto, and Charon formed a triple planet system with a distinct
  orbit around the Sun. Then one day, the aliens came along,
  grabbed hold of Triton, and pushed it into a retrograde orbit
  around the planet Neptune. In route to Neptune, Pluto and Charon
  hung on for a while, then broke loose and drifted off into a new
  orbit. When did this happen? St. George says the aliens were
  here in 580 A.D., so that would be his guess for the date of
  these planet manipulations.
  I mentioned that I had read on the Internet that Pluto has been
  downgraded, that it is no longer considered a planet. St. George
  responded: "I believe that was because they found that Pluto
  didn't clear away debris in its orbit. But since 580 A.D., a
  contemporary date in terms of solar system history, Pluto in its
  new orbit would have made only a handful of complete orbits
  around the Sun, hardly enough time to clear away much debris. In
  any case, the astronomers got it all wrong. What they should
  really be looking for is Triton's original orbit, a cleared-out
  orbit with no planet in it. And I doubt that we're talking about
  an orbit at the outer edges of the solar system. Triton's
  original orbit may have been closer to the Sun than Neptune.
  They need to figure out where Triton could have been in 580
  A.D., then they will know where to look for that orbit."
  Why did the aliens move Triton? A display of power? St. George
  remarked that the star arrow only provides longitudinal
  coordinates. We also need to know the latitude . The planets
  have to be in the right position at the right time. And the
  three stars too, for that matter.
  The last stanza of the three stanzas is numbered IV-33. It
  begins: Jupiter closer to Venus than to the Moon, appearing in
  full whiteness. According to St. George, Earth and Jupiter would
  have to be pretty much on opposite sides of the Sun for this to
  be true, and the full Moon (more likely seen from the Alien
  Planet than from Earth) serves as a timer. The alignment is
  Alien Planet, Sun, Moon.
  The next line of IV-33 goes: Venus hidden under the whiteness
  Neptune (discovered more than two hundred years after the death
  of Nostradamus). Note that there's no "of" between whiteness and
  Neptune. Meanwhile, the French words following "hidden" (used
  elsewhere in the prophecies to cryptic ends), "soUS la
  bANcheUR," allows the extraction of "Uranus." Thus, the
  whiteness (partial rather than full) is Uranus, not Neptune, and
  we have a second alignment: Alien Planet, Uranus, Venus.
  IV-33 has one more line: From Mars struck through the white
  granary. Since Neptune was left hanging at the end of the
  preceding line, it should come into play here, meaning Neptune
  from Mars struck through the white granary. According to St.
  George, the "white granary" refers to a star cluster called the
  Pleiades, which happens to lie at the opposite side of the sky
  from Barnard 72. Until recently, St. George thought the
  planetary arrow to Barnard 72 commenced with Mars, so he not yet
  had a chance to check out if a Mars, Neptune, Pleiades
  alignment, or a Pleiades, Mars, Neptune alignment, is even
  feasible.
  Overall, there are only a limited number of possibilities. IV-33
  gives us two inner planets, Venus and Mars, and two outer
  planets, Uranus and Neptune. Mars lines up with Neptune to hit
  the Pleiades, and Venus lines up with Uranus to hit the Alien
  Planet. Depending upon the Pleiades direction, Uranus and
  Neptune need to be together on the same side of the solar system
  or on directly opposing ends of the solar system. Also remember
  to check that you're viewing a full Moon from the Alien Planet,
  and that Jupiter is closer to Venus than the Moon at the same
  time. When? The skies and planets are in constant motion. In
  what year does all this happen?
  St. George is convinced that the date of the given configuration
  should somehow or somewhere be provided in the prophecies. Other
  than the stanza number, 433, we have 580, 700, 703, 882, 883,
  1204, 1559, 1571, 1607, 1609, 1649, 1666, 1689, 1690, 1700,
  1727, 1781, 1813, 1832, 1858, 1859, 1861, 1928, 1952, 1955,
  1979, 1982, 1999, 2001, and 2006. The years 1571, 1607, 1781,
  1859, and 1982 were astronomy related. St. George suspects one
  of the later years is more likely mainly because astronomers may


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m24-006.shtml[12/12/2011 09:15:45]
Where SETI Astronomers Can Find Aliens

  not have accurate data the position of the outer planets in
  earlier times. "We have to assume that they want us to get it
  right, and precision is clearly required here."
  2006? What happened in 2006? St. George replied: "Absolutely
  nothing. 2006 was a second, inferable date in a London
  catastrophe stanza. The date does not necessarily have to come
  from an astronomy stanza. It can be provided elsewhere."
  Please excuse the digression. My final question was: Do you
  realistically expect SETI astronomers to take you up on this
  coordinate stuff? St. George responded: "Yes. It would be
  foolish of them not to. The way they're going now, their odds of
  finding E.T. are not even one in a billion. If my theories
  merely reduce the odds to one in a thousand, their chances
  improve immensely. Moreover, I think they've forgotten; SETI was
  originally based on the premise that there are lots of
  intelligent civilizations out there, which in turn implies that
  at least one of them should have succeeded in exploring the
  entire galaxy by now."
  So there you have it, SETI astronomers, go forth and become
  famous, work out the coordinates, point your radio telescope
  there, and tell the world you heard from E.T.!

  About the Author
  By Gersiane De Brito with special thanks to Morten St. George
  and:
  http://www.crypticthinking.com

                                           Triangular UFO Over Caracas Venezuela
  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 08:14:02 -0500
  Fwd Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 21:51:20 -0500
  Subject: Triangular UFO Over Caracas Venezuela


  Source: Archivos Forteanos Latinoamericanos
  Date: 11/24/06
  Venezuela: Triangular UFO Over Caracas
  A report from Hector Escalante
  CARACAS - November 2006. Three people witnessed the transit of a
  triangular UFO on November 16 as it passed over a state banking
  institution located on Av. Urdaneta, bordering the central
  district of Caracas, the Venezuelan capital.
  According to information provided by Israel Urbaneja, the
  appearance of this strange object lasted from 9:30 to 10:00 PM
  approximately, allowing two of his relatives to join the
  observation from their home on Av. Baralt.
  Likewise, he said that the object "was white in color but
  presented luminous variations of blue, red and green" and moved
  with a "zig-zagging" motion from south to north over the capital
  area's airspace until it became lost in the clouds, which was
  present at all times, althought with various degrees of
  clearing, accompanied by heavy rains earlier during the day.
  "This is the first time that I've seen anything like it and I'm
  certain it wasn't an airplane or satellite by the way it moved.
  Furthermore, the object left a glowing, cone-shaped white wake
  as it flew, which caused a sensation akin to nausea," said the
  witness.
  It should be noticed that this is not the first time that an
  unknown object with intelligent behavior has been seen over the
  central district of the Venezuelan capital, where major
  government offices are located.
  Other witnesses have reported the presence of similar objects
  near the presidential palace and Fort Tiuna (army garrison) on
  Paseo de los Proceres, as well as in the vicinity of the
  majestic El Avila National Park to the north of Caracas.
  -----
  Translator's note - the health effects produced by flybys of
  these triangular objects have been reported in other cases, both
  in the US and abroad.

  From: Scott Corrales <lornis1.nul>
  Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 09:18:23 -0500
  Fwd Date: Fri, 24 Nov 2006 21:54:09 -0500
  Subject: UFO Over Spain's Canary Islands?

  The Journal of Hispanic Ufology
  November 23, 2006
  Source: Canarias 24 Horas
  http://tinyurl.com/yx3o66
  Date: 11.22.06
  TENERIFE - A number of phone calls have been received by this
  newsroom from the Tacoronte sector in northern Tenerife,
  reporting - not without a degree of nervousness - sightings of
  strange lights on Tuesday evening. Some of the witnesses have
  spoken openly of UFOs. Those who claim having witnessed this
  phenomenon report that even household appliances have died for a
  few seconds and others report seeing static white lights diving
  into the Tacorontan coast.
  This is hardly the first time that various witnesses report
  seeing "strange" things in the sky, moving at high speed among
  the stars or emerging from the bottom of the sea.
  According to experts consulted by Canarias24horas.com, the
  lights are nothing more than satellites, which give the
  impression of being stars despite their rapid movement. The
  lights entering and exiting the ocean are interpreted by some as
  large shooting stars that never reach the Earth's surface and
  vanish into the horizon; some reports mentioned green, blue and
  red lights - colors proper to a shooting star as it enters our
  atmosphere. As far as what was seen on Tuesday, the evidence
  points to a series of helicopters which were flying over the
  area. Two of these late model aircraft were surveying the
  coastline between northern Tenerife and the island of La Palma.
  But what caused the household appliances to fail? The
  explanation is a simple one, and appears to be connected to the
  impending visit of Their Majesties the King and Queen of Spain
  to the Canaries.
  This isn't the first that the passing of a royal motorcade on a
  highway causes all appliances liable to perceive or emit radio
  signals to stop working for a few seconds. Refrigerators also
  shut down. This effect is produced by devices known as signal
  inhibitors, which mask anything that could represent a safety
  hazard to a head of state. Iceboxes shut down because they
  signal inhibitors cannot distinguish between one appliance and
  another. Even the Internet is disconnected.
  Could this be the answer to the experiences of Tacoronte's
  residents on Tuesday? We can only say that for the Royal
  Family's security detail, shutting off devices at a distance is
  mere childs' play.

  Good Morning, Ed, List, All -
  From the 509th Unit History for July 1947:
  Commercial Transportation Office, transferred under Squadron
  "T", issued 160 travel requests, 350 meal tickets, 180 out-bound
  bills, 160 in-bound bills of lading, 8 overseas shipments, and
  handled 100,000 pounds of air freight.
  Supervisor of Transportation reported successful improvement in
  vehicle maintenance and indoctrination of drivers to their
  responsibilities.
  A squadron party was held at Bottomless Lakes, Friday 11 July
  1947...
  Squadron T was the transportation squadron and the above gives a
  hint as to their functions. Notice that none of those functions
  come under the heading of military police... though their
  mechanics would be responsible for the maintenance of the
  military police vehicles.

  UFOs, The Anomalous Phenomenon
  bu UFO Secrets
  There are many things that can't be explained to this day. The
  disappearance of ships and planes in the Bermuda Triangle, the
  origin of Stonehenge in the United Kingdom and if UFOs really
  exist.
  No one has yet been able to come up with a logical explanation
  for any of these which as created a lot of speculation of the
  existence of beings in the universe.
  Some say aliens captured those who entered the Bermuda triangle.
  Stonehenge was a marker left by beings from a different planet
  and that UFOs are making observations of those on Earth for an
  impending invasion soon to come.
  These rumors have no basis whatsoever which is why the
  scientific community doesn't put that much attention to them and
  give priority to other things such as cures for diseases and the
  evolution of man.
  The reason why some of the sightings are considered hoaxes is
  because they were reported by people who are hysterical and have
  been inconsistent in the past. Though a majority of these cases
  have been explained, there is still a smaller percentage that
  still needs to be analyzed.
  These are the ones witnessed by doctors, military personnel, law
  enforcement officers and ordinary professionals who have nothing
  to lose and believe that the incidents really took place.
  This has made even some of the most brilliant people question
  the possibility and in turn created a field of study called
  Ufology. There are other organizations that have been
  established all over the world who continue to believe that
  UFOs really exist.
  Despite the government's inquiry many years ago, there are many
  incidents that haven't been explained. Records procured because
  of the US Freedom of Information Act will show of times that
  weapon systems didn't work when fighter planes were sent to
  intercept the UFOs or how the flybys of these alien spacecraft
  caused disruptions in military installations.
  The government can try to hide the truth but this can only go so
  far. This has been the motivation of those who choose to believe
  and will continue with the struggle until the secret has been
  revealed.

Has UFO Phenomena Become Common Place?

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
                                               'Its All Here In Black & White'

                                       Has UFO Phenomena Become Common Place?
  From: Greg Boone <Evolbaby.nul>
  Date: Sun, 26 Nov 2006 10:40:01 EST
  Fwd Date: Sun, 26 Nov 2006 17:10:22 -0500
  Subject: Has UFO Phenomena Become Common Place?

  I've had to realize something recently. Quite a big cognition
  regarding the reality of the UFO phenom and it's offshoots.
  I study a wide array of sciences and subjects and I get emails
  from not only this List but dozens and dozens ranging from
  art to history, news, music, religion and on and on.
  In the other areas of non-UFO interest I've noticed over the
  years that UFO stories will turn up in every one of the other
  areas of interests.
  Then I realized that the stories of sightings and abductions are
  now so common, so permeating the general global culture that I
  would read or hear about more UFO-related stories than stories
  about good gas mileage or weight loss problems!
  I mean it's really gotten so commonplace it's losing or lost
  it's mystery factor!
  I never thought I'd see the day when I could literally sit here
  and see this subject of UFOs so run-of-the-mill that the fear
  factor has waned.
  People know the drill cold! I guess it's all the books and
  lectures and TV specials and radio programs that you all have
  been part of or produced. I truly believe it's become so
  accepted as part of our lives and the government non-compliance
  with addressing the issue has really sunk in as we who spend
  much time investigating it already know.
  This common acceptance has grown over the years. I've mentioned
  it before but nowadays it's just astounding to see!
  I don't think it's a major task anymore to convince people it's
  real, what is needed is what to do when one encounters a UFO
  event. Maybe it's the disclosures of how government operates
  these past post 9/11 years that has opened the public's eyes or
  just the saturation of UFO data thanks to the availability of
  the internet. Whatever it is I find it no longer a chore nor
  challenge to discuss the matter with people. They'll bring up
  the subject without my chiding or prodding and they'll discuss
  it as casually as they'll discuss the latest new lawnmower.
  Somehow, somewhere, the old stigma has or is wearing off. Maybe
  soon we'll have more breaking stories and data.
  Worth keeping a weather eye out for.

  Best,
  Greg

                                                        Mystery Of Orange UFOs
  From: UFO UpDates - Toronto <ufoupdates.nul>
  Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2006 07:16:33 -0500
  Fwd Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2006 07:16:33 -0500
  Subject: Mystery Of Orange UFOs


  Source: The Argus -             Brighton, UK
  http://tinyurl.com/y6uqlk
  November 27, 2006

  Mystery Of Orange UFOs
  By Andy Dickenson
  Bright lights in the skies have baffled police and air-traffic
  controllers.
  The unidentified flying objects have been likened to similar
  strange orange glows seen over Liverpool and Essex.
  Witnesses said thousands of people may have seen the bizarre
  floating orbs.
  Air-traffic controllers at Shoreham Airport and Brighton police
  said they had received inquiries about the UFOs, with as many as
  eight seen in the sky at one time.
  James Gordon-Johnson, of Preston Park Avenue, Brighton, said he
  was leaving a restaurant in Shoreham with his brother at 11.30pm
  on November 18 when he saw "what appeared to be a very big
  orange light in the sky".
  He added: "It was very, very bright but static - it wasn't
  rising or falling. Another one then appeared in mid-air. Then
  another.
  "It must have been somewhere over Hove Lagoon but the lights
  were so bright thousands of people must have seen them.
  "The next morning I got a phone call from a friend of mine who
  saw the exact same thing."
  Mark Sztopel, from Brighton, told The Argus he saw seven lights
  moving slowly in an easterly direction across the city at
  midnight.
  He added: "I'm a big plane enthusiast so I know what the lights
  and characteristics of a plane look like at night, and I can
  tell you now that these definitely weren't planes."
  A spokeswoman for Shoreham Airport said staff had received
  emails from people inquiring about the glowing objects.
  She said: "We closed at 7pm so there was nothing happening here.
  We've no idea what they could have been."
  Police said they also received a report from a man in Hove who
  said he saw "approximately eight planes coming in over the sea,
  with no flashing navigation lights, towards Gatwick, in a dead
  line".


http://www.ufoupdateslist.com/2006/nov/m27-002.shtml[12/12/2011 09:16:37]
Mystery Of Orange UFOs

  Officers contacted air traffic controllers at Gatwick who said
  they knew of no movement in the area.
  Sue Heard, a police spokeswoman, said: "We were called out and
  made checks to establish it wasn't a known aircraft.
  "It certainly seems pretty baffling on the face of it but there
  was a meteor shower on Saturday so maybe the two are connected."
  A cloud of comet dust produced a Leonids meteor shower over the
  weekend, which managers of Herstmonceux Observatory said peaked
  on Saturday night with a display of shooting stars.
  UFO spotters have also linked the orange lights to sightings in
  Liverpool and Essex, recently revealed as hoaxes created using
  open flames suspended under plastic bags to produce mini hot-air
  balloons.
  But Mr Gordon-Johnson, 33, said: "These weren't meteors -
   there's no way they were meteors. They were far too big and
  bright and low in the atmosphere.
  "They looked like they were about 3,000 or 4,000ft up. As I kept
  looking at them they just sat there. I was trying to think of
  explanations but couldn't think of one.
  "It was very odd. If it was just a balloon you wouldn't have
  seen another just appear at the same altitude. There was no
  sound. Nothing at all."
  Do you know anything about these strange lights in the sky? Call
  The Argus on 01273 544538 or email andy.dickenson.nul

  John Frick writes on the Mothman Lives e-mail List:
  >As far as Keel being a demonologist. He really isn't as far as I
  >know. Keel has mentioned that the UFO and MIB phenomena is tied
  >into demonology, but I've never read him claim to be an actual
  >demonologist. From all the reading I have done on Keel he seemed
  >to think demons came from the same source as ghosts and UFOs.
  "Ufology is just another name for demonology," John Keel told
  me, a week before the September 11th attack on the World Trade
  Center, which occurred just a couple of miles from where he
  lives.
  - Loren Coleman, in Mothman and Other Curious Encounters, page
  114, (NY: Paraview, 2002).

  Jerome Clark has noted that Keel's speculations placed him
  closer to being an occultist, and has written that Keel is
  "nothing so much as a demonologist."
  Clark goes on: "Whereas traditional ufologists took a relatively
  conservative approach, seeking testimony from trained observers
  and putting a premium on radar/visual and multiply-witnessed
  sightings, and viewed exotic claims with suspicion, Keel
  vigorously championed everything from Mothman to contactees.
  Many ufologists doubted that the former a monstrous birdlike
  entity reported over a several month period by persons living
  along the Ohio River had anything to do with UFOs, and they had
  long ranked the latter (individuals who claimed ongoing
  communications with friendly extraterrestrials) among the
  crooked and the crazy.
  Keel, however, argued that 'ultraterrestrials' supernatural
  'transmogrifications' of paranormal energy from an unimaginable
  other reality have been pestering, frightening, manipulating,
  and even destroying human beings from the beginning of mankind=B9s
  history.'
  - Loren Coleman, in Mothman and Other Curious Encounters, pages
  118-119, (NY: Paraview, 2002).

  Although the publisher deleted my direct references to Clark's
  quotes, they did retain my bibliography; one can locate these
  quotations through these sources:
  Clark, Jerome. "Mothman." Encyclopedia of Strange and
  Unexplained Physical Phenomena. Detroit: Gale, 1993, pp.
  228--231.
  "Keel, John Alva." The UFO Encyclopedia 2nd Edition: The
  Phenomenon from the Beginning, Volume 1. Detroit: Omnigraphics,
  1998, pp. 550--552.

Not By Chance

                                   A mailing list for the study of UFO-related phenomena
